result.title: Delegating Earth science model calibration to knowledge-guided LLM agents
result.summary: Applying process-based Earth science models to new sites and questions often requires expert calibration decisions. Reliable delegation to language-model agents must preserve scientific competence and reproducibility. Here we develop a general calibration harness (GCH) for end-to-end delegation from a calibration request to assessed results. Constrained by a knowledge infrastructure (KI) and a validation convention, agents define parameter domains, observation mappings and objectives, and generate model-specific code. GCH checks the formulations against the same declarations and freezes them before numerical search and assessment, which require no further agent judgement. Agent-authored workflows executed across six model families, with assessment identifying unmet criteria. In snow-model tests, five of five knowledge-guided specifications executed on the first attempt, compared with none of five given only the model name, achieving validation Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) of 0.81-0.94 against 0.57 for defaults. Under a common objective, independent GR4J formulations yielded scores within 0.001 NSE; re-evaluating eleven saved parameter vectors reproduced their metrics. In ten paired VIC tests with matched budgets, fixed search was non-inferior to continuing agent proposals (margin, -0.02 NSE; median difference, -0.003). This separation enables end-to-end calibration delegation with inspectable scientific choices and reproducible numerical evaluation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出通用标定框架 GCH，将地球科学过程模型的标定端到端委托给知识约束下的 LLM agent：由 agent 定义参数域、观测映射与目标并生成模型代码，冻结声明后再进行数值搜索与评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「匹配预算下固定搜索不劣于继续采纳 agent 提议」的结论可能与 LVR 中动态计算、停止决策的收益成本权衡相关；「先冻结规格再搜索」的设计也可能为核查推理状态生成与评估分离提供线索。
